answer: VDF-paced identity issuance with bonded deposits resists sybils. Each identity computes a verifiable delay function costing fixed wall-clock time and posts a small bond. The delay can't be parallelized, so attackers cannot mint thousands of identities to wander through governance overnight: it needs thousands of cores for days plus capital each. Timing forensics slash correlated bursts, turning bot farms from cheap pigment into one target. Honest users pay once in time; attackers pay time, capital, risk: the sable line. Limits: slower onboarding, trusted custody, rich attackers still can.
